o1.biggest_strength: Every ad set gets a rupee verdict and the three owner signals (revive the paused creator video, split out women 25-34, kill the COD-trap Starter Kit) are all caught and priced.
o1.biggest_mistake: The two break-even lines (₹282 safe / ₹394 break-even) are a clever device but the per-ad-set safe numbers in the table aren't shown to be derived consistently, so a finance-minded reader has to trust them.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Show the safe/break-even math per ad set in one column each (order value × COD mix × 72% haircut) so the table is auditable, and trim the creative section slightly to keep the budget and rules the spine.

o2.biggest_strength: The reserve-release rules and the retargeting holdout test are genuinely owner-grade thinking, and the forecast lines (store-count vs Meta-count) frame the decision honestly.
o2.biggest_mistake: It cuts retargeting (frequency 6.8 is a real signal but ₹289 cost vs ₹358 profit per order is the one ad set that clearly pays) and spreads the fix across too many conditional branches, so the one-page decision is harder to act on Monday morning.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Simplify to one committed number per ad set with a single reserve rule, and keep the retargeting holdout as a clearly optional appendix rather than mixing it into the main call.

reason: Both are strong and both catch the three real signals, but Output 1 is the one I can hand to my team Monday: every ad set has one verdict, the budget table adds to ₹5,60,000 cleanly, and the rules are numbered and short. Output 2 is smarter on the holdout test but I have to work harder to find the single decision.
